root_cause.text: The `p2pmem_alloc_mmap()` function in the PCI P2PDMA subsystem incorrectly asserts that the initial reference count of an allocated page is non-zero using `!page_ref_count(page)`, triggering a kernel warning when `CONFIG_DEBUG_VM` is enabled because a previous commit changed the initial refcount of P2PDMA pages from one to zero.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the assertion in `drivers/pci/p2pdma.c` being corrected from `VM_WARN_ON_ONCE_PAGE(!page_ref_count(page), page)` to `VM_WARN_ON_ONCE_PAGE(page_ref_count(page), page)` to reflect that the expected initial reference count of the allocated page is zero.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix an inverted logic bug in p2pmem_alloc_mmap to correctly warn when an allocated page has an unexpected non-zero reference count.
intent_record.what: The condition in VM_WARN_ON_ONCE_PAGE is changed from checking if the page reference count is zero (!page_ref_count(page)) to checking if it is non-zero (page_ref_count(page)).
intent_record.how: This ensures the kernel correctly warns when a newly allocated page unexpectedly has an active reference count before its count is initialized, rather than warning when it is correctly zero.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces the incorrect assertion `VM_WARN_ON_ONCE_PAGE(!page_ref_count(page), page);` in `drivers/pci/p2pdma.c`. Since the page reference count is now initialized to 0, `!page_ref_count(page)` evaluates to true, triggering a kernel warning when `CONFIG_DEBUG_VM` is enabled. The correct assertion should have checked if the refcount was non-zero (i.e., `VM_WARN_ON_ONCE_PAGE(page_ref_count(page), page)`).
